clue.text: Roan landing at a mix-up here

definitions.text: Roan landing at a mix-up here

indicators.note: a mix-up is a jumble, so the letters of the three words before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A roan horse comes down after a jump and causes chaos at the big steeplechase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mix-up' rearranges ROAN LANDING AT. The whole clue is also the definition: a horse falling at a fence into a pile-up is a classic sight at Aintree's famous race.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand National is Britain's best-known steeplechase, run at Aintree, where falls and pile-ups at fences are notorious.

indicators.note: the word for winged sits inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
alate is a botanical and zoological term meaning having wings

explanation.surface: A winged nymph is spotted somewhere in Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: ALATE, a technical word for winged, goes inside GA.
explanation.definitionFit: Galatea is a sea nymph of Greek myth, loved by the Cyclops Polyphemus.

clue.text: Being a messenger was once worth something

definitions.meaning: a heavenly being sent with a message from God
an old English gold coin stamped with St Michael, no longer in use

explanation.walkthrough: The angel was an English gold coin of the 15th to 17th centuries, hence 'was once worth something'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek root means messenger, so a spiritual envoy fits the first; an obsolete gold coin fits the second.

parts.note: a railway fog signal placed on the line bangs when a wheel passes over it, and an explosive cap sets off a charge

explanation.surface: A railway signalman wears a noisy hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Railwaymen once clipped small explosive devices to the rails as fog warnings; the same word names the cap that sets off a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A fog signal on the railway is a small explosive charge, and a percussion cap is the device that triggers a blast.

parts.note: money staked on a game or race is a bet

explanation.surface: Putting a bit on a horse is called a kind of investment.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or encourage, usually in wrongdoing, so it is a verb synonym of aid.

clue.text: Vex by introducing girl to a mysterious rite

indicators.note: introducing the girl to the rite means putting her name inside its letters
a mysterious word is obscure in form, so the letters of rite are scrambled

parts.note: Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone annoys others by bringing a young woman into a strange ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mysterious' scrambles RITE to IRTE, and 'introducing' puts RITA inside it: IR-RITA-TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To irritate is to annoy, a straight synonym of vex.

clue.text: It's more pleasant back in the precinct

indicators.note: back says the letters found are read from right to left
in says the letters sit inside the words the precinct

explanation.surface: Things are better back at the police precinct.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'the precinct' backwards and NICER appears across 'precinct'; 'back' gives the turnaround and 'in' the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicer is the comparative of nice, meaning more agreeable.

parts.note: the Liberals, abbreviated Lib, are a minor party in British politics
a ration is a fixed allowance or share

explanation.surface: A minor political party gets its allotted share of votes or seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A swinging' is a noun phrase: libration is an oscillation, as of the Moon seeming to rock as seen from Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Libration is an oscillating motion, especially the apparent rocking of the Moon, so it is a swaying movement.

parts.note: something oval-shaped like a hen's product, which has gone off, describes a rotten person

explanation.surface: A football yob at the Oval cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground, but here oval simply describes the shape of an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad egg is an idiom for a disreputable or troublesome person, and an egg is oval.

clue.text: Easy time a long way off ?

parts.note: light work is easy work
a year is a period of time

explanation.surface: An undemanding spell of time lies far in the future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time' suggests the answer measures time, but it is a distance: how far light travels in twelve months.
explanation.definitionFit: This unit of astronomical distance is used for stars very far from Earth.

parts.note: a cob is a hazelnut, so nutty gives the nut
RA, Royal Academician, is a standard crossword painter

explanation.surface: A crazy artist is attacked by a creature from Kipling.
explanation.walkthrough: Rikki-Tikki-Tavi is the mongoose hero of a Kipling story who kills snakes. 'Nutty' wants to mean mad but gives COB, a cobnut.
explanation.definitionFit: In Kipling's Jungle Book story the mongoose fights and kills the snakes Nag and Nagaina, both hooded serpents.

definitions.meaning: an ancient unit of weight, and of money, in Greece and the Middle East

explanation.walkthrough: The sense of natural ability comes from the Bible's parable of the servants given silver measured by this ancient weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift is a natural ability, and the same word was an ancient measure of mass used for silver.

clue.text: Use a telescope in the cinema?

definitions.text: Use a telescope in the cinema?

parts.words: Use a telescope in the cinema?
parts.note: looking at celestial bodies through a lens, or gawping at film celebrities on the screen

explanation.surface: Someone takes a telescope into a film show.
explanation.walkthrough: Film celebrities are called stars, so gazing at the screen is gazing at stars.
explanation.definitionFit: To look at the heavens is the literal sense; staring at film celebrities is the punning one.

clue.text: Concedes there are about a thousand approaches

indicators.note: the approaches are wrapped about the letter for a thousand

parts.note: adits are horizontal entrances or approaches to a mine
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone owns up that there are roughly a thousand routes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'roughly' but puts ADITS around M.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit is to acknowledge or confess, so the verb matches concedes.

clue.text: Handy for the painter and his playful dog ?

definitions.text: Handy for the painter and his playful dog ?

parts.words: Handy for the painter and his playful dog ?
parts.note: a rod an artist rests the brush hand on, and a stick a frisky dog mauls

explanation.surface: Something useful for an artist, and for his frisky pet.
explanation.walkthrough: The painter's rest steadies the hand; a playful dog would maul a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A mahlstick is a long padded rod a painter uses to steady the brush hand, here read as a stick for a dog to maul.

definitions.meaning: holding back development, as of a plant or child
performing daring tricks in an aircraft

explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Stunting means retarding growth, and also doing stunts, the word for aerial tricks.

definitions.meaning: the famous black horse of the highwayman Dick Turpin, a female horse as dark as the night

explanation.walkthrough: Black Bess was the horse of English highwayman Dick Turpin; a black female horse is a 'night mare'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad dream is the ordinary sense; split, it is a dark-coloured female horse like Turpin's.

parts.note: raised decoration made by beating metal from the back

explanation.surface: Someone gets respite from a constant pounding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relief' wants to mean respite, but it is the art term for raised work.
explanation.definitionFit: Repoussé metalwork is ornament raised in relief by hammering the reverse side of a sheet.

parts.note: a horse speeds up when the rider digs in the pointed heel devices this maker sells

explanation.surface: Horses are keen on what a certain tradesman makes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go for' reads as 'like', but horses go faster when spurred.
explanation.definitionFit: A spurrier is a maker of spurs, the pointed heel devices that urge a horse on.

definitions.meaning: a source of water rising from the ground
the season that comes ahead of summer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' is the noun for a water source, not the adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural water source is a spring, and the season preceding summer is spring.

parts.note: to age is to mature

indicators.note: moving letters around means rearranging the word and

explanation.surface: Something both grown-up and touching is on the schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' looks like 'touching' but rearranges AND to NDA.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items to be dealt with, a schedule or plan.

indicators.note: the word are goes within the insects

parts.note: worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: Communist labourers are inside, under the red star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red star' and 'workers' suggest a Soviet scene; the star is real and ARE sits within ANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Antares is the bright reddish supergiant in Scorpius.

clue.text: Oppose gold for a set piece

parts.note: to resist is to oppose
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Someone fights against gold in a planned move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set piece' sounds like a football move, but it is a component of a radio or television set.
explanation.definitionFit: A resistor is a component in an electrical circuit, a part of a wireless or TV set.

definitions.meaning: the queen of this land was famed for testing Solomon's wisdom; the name came to mean a wise or alluring woman
an ancient realm in southern Arabia

explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen of Sheba matched wits with Solomon, giving a byword for a shrewd woman, and Sheba was an ancient Arabian realm.

definitions.meaning: being present at a Test match, split as two words
to bear witness to or confirm

explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match, so a spectator is 'at Test'; 'it' rounds off the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to certify or bear witness; split, it describes a spectator at a Test match.

indicators.note: variations on the word three are other orders of its letters

explanation.surface: A broadcasting channel carries three different versions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variations' rearranges THREE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ether was once thought to be the substance filling space through which light and radio waves travel.

clue.text: In which playing hooky may land one in trouble?

definitions.text: In which playing hooky may land one in trouble?

parts.words: In which playing hooky may land one in trouble?
parts.note: hitting a shot that curves left lands the ball in a bunker or rough

explanation.surface: Skipping school may get you into bother.
explanation.walkthrough: Playing hooky is American for truancy, but here a hook is a stroke that curves off line into a hazard.
explanation.definitionFit: In this game a hooked drive veers off course and may finish in trouble such as rough, trees or a bunker.

clue.text: This is one form of disturbance

indicators.note: a form of the words is one is a new shape made from their letters

explanation.surface: Someone describes a particular kind of commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges IS ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise is unwanted sound, and a din is a type of disruption.

clue.text: Her mascot makes the front cover

indicators.note: makes says the letters of her mascot are made into something new

explanation.surface: A woman's lucky charm appears on the front of a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges HER MASCOT. 'front cover' suggests a magazine, but it is clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A stomacher was a decorative triangular panel worn over the chest and belly at the front of a bodice.

parts.note: a rogue who wins over lovers is a scoundrel in matters of love, and also a playing card

explanation.surface: The famous seducer has his own playing card.
explanation.walkthrough: Casanova, the Venetian seducer, is a rogue of romance; the court card is the jack of the red suit with the heart symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is a rogue, and Casanova a scoundrel with women; the same name is a court card in the deck.
